look_here_first: TEXAS SIGNALGRASS: the new close-up now shows multiple ASCENDING branches lined with comparatively large elongate green spikelets (about 4.5–5.9 mm in UT records). On a separately collected ripe spikelet, lower glume typically reaches about HALF to TWO-THIRDS of spikelet length. Don't turn a CC-licensed photo or wide grass clump into confirmed glume lengths without a ruler. TEXAS SIGNALGRASS SECOND DIAGNOSTIC PASS: once a whole head and its large one-sided ascending branches are recognized, confirm on the SAME plant: a 1–1.8 mm membranous ligule with ciliate fringe at opened collar, actual ~4.5–5.9 mm mature spikelets, and lower glume ~2.4–3.2 mm (roughly half to two-thirds of total spikelet). A paired spikelet may be missing because one sibling aborts. Lift both glumes and separate the lower staminate floret from the upper bisexual hard ridged lemma under a 10–20× hand lens. These are field measurements from UT treatment, NOT visible/scaled claims for gallery pixels.

learner_visual_status.note: Four physically archived source-labelled U. texana JPEGs: two habit/panicle views plus two USDA public-domain spikelet and floret/grain plates with printed mm scales. The seven-panel teaching gallery also contains three labelled other-species comparisons. Remaining essential species evidence: true 1–1.8 mm ciliate membranous ligule at the inner blade/sheath junction, a connected rooted Hays-area flowering annual, and if vein counts are taught, a sufficiently resolved same-specimen glume/lemma dissection. Existing anatomy plate is REAL, not merely a research-only reference; source photo rights and mobile arrow QA remain separate.

best_field_traits: Warm-season native Texas grass; often an annual tuft of soft relatively broad foliage.
Terminal panicle generally with multiple alternate ascending principal branches, often 4 or more.
Spikelets distinctively large for this 3-way comparison, about 4.5–6 mm long; single or paired at branch nodes.
Lower glume often reaches near middle to ~two-thirds spikelet, unlike much smaller basal glumes of U. fusca or U. reptans.
Very short stalked spikelets, lower floret male/sterile and upper floret fertile; upper fertile lemma firm and finely cross-wrinkled.
True ligule and sheath anatomy need macro confirmation and should never be fabricated from habitat overview.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Panicle close-up with ascending branches in frame
Mature 4.5–6 mm ovoid spikelet beside mm scale
Attached lower glume measuring about half to two-thirds spikelet length
Dissect lower male floret versus upper tough fertile lemma
Leaf collar, ligule, blade width with ruler
Full habit including basal rooted tuft
crew_field_check: START with the NEW credited Texas panicle image, not the original crowded landscape shot: see intact spikelet-bearing ascending branches.
MEASURE mature spikelets beside millimeter ruler: 4.5–5.9 mm is described by the UT Plant Resources Center.
Peel one intact ripe spikelet to isolate LOWER glume about half to two-thirds its length and UPPER glume near its tip (both actual veins/lengths need macro).
Photograph the lower staminate/sterile floret separately from the upper hard fertile lemma; some outer bracts have conspicuous cross-veins.
Check true collar for a membranous/ciliate ligule, then compare shorter-spikeleted U. fusca and U. reptans. If immature/unmeasured, report Urochloa sp.

comparisons.key_distinctions: The new Commons panicle photo reveals the real, larger green units; compare with smaller U. fusca (~2.4–3.4 mm, lower glume ~1/4–1/3) and small U. reptans (~1.5–2.2 mm, lower glume ~1/8–1/4). Texas signalgrass has an alternate-branch panicle and a short membranous, ciliate ligule, but the close-up shows no exposed collar or dissected floret.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare 5–10 ripe attached spikelets, exposed lower glumes and the inner ligules on two source-confirmed plants.
field_matrix.separating_characters: Texas U. texana is much larger: ripe spikelets ~4.5–5.9 mm, lower glume ~2.4–3.2 mm (roughly half to two-thirds), upper glume ~4.5–5.6 mm, and a ciliate membranous ligule ~1–1.8 mm. Brownseed U. fusca has ~2.4–3.4 mm spikelets, a shorter lower glume (~1–1.3 mm in UT) and a true ligule consisting of a short hair fringe. Both have hard rugose upper fertile lemmas without a long awn.
field_matrix.caution: The existing USDA plate shows real U. texana reproductive anatomy, but its resolution does not justify fine vein-count arrows; confirm lower-glume veins with a higher-resolution dissection.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Lay mature spikelets and their lower glumes at identical magnification, then open the actual collar rather than photographing sheath hairs alone.
field_matrix.separating_characters: U. texana spikelets ~4.5–5.9 mm and lower glumes ~2.4–3.2 mm dwarf U. reptans (~1.5–2.2 mm spikelets; lower glume ~0.2–0.6 mm or 1/8–1/4). Texana has a ciliate membranous ligule ~1–1.8 mm; reptans has a short hair-fringe ligule. Rooting low nodes are not an exclusive separator because both annuals can produce them.
field_matrix.caution: Do not use a whole-head silhouette or the mere presence of nodal roots as a final species test; the two true ligules and lower glumes need real measured photos.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Texas signalgrass: adult branch → dorsal and ventral spikelet glumes → fertile floret/grain; true ligule remains
steps: PHOTO WALK: display all four physically archived Texas signalgrass views first—general habitat, actual Sam Kieschnick panicle, USDA front/back spikelets with mm ticks, then USDA fertile florets and grains. Only AFTER these use the DIFFERENT-SPECIES U. fusca and U. reptans comparison panels.
1. Start with real photographed full seedhead (Sam Kieschnick panicle) and separate ascending terminal branches carrying ovoid spikelets on one side; avoid interpreting raceme color as species proof.

2. Compare species source-photo habit view with a real plant base. Texas signalgrass is a warm-season annual: photograph both fibrous roots and whether lower trailing nodes have adventitious roots (Williamson County treatment).

3. At one LEAF junction gently open the upper sheath to expose the TRUE 1–1.8 mm ciliate membranous ligule. The white hairy collar and blade-base hairs are nearby but not identical to the membrane; take macro with 1-mm ruler.

4. Photograph three adult spikelets face-on and edge-on beside a real 1-mm scale. UT describes 4.5–5.9 mm long, distinctly larger than U. fusca or U. reptans; do NOT measure from uncalibrated site image.

5. Follow the branching axis and sample each node: spikelets frequently occur in unequal PAIRS; a single unit can represent an aborted partner, so single appearance is not evidence against Urochloa texana.

6. Open one mature spikelet (not detached bracts from different specimens): the LOWER ovate glume is 2.4–3.2 mm and around half to two-thirds of entire spikelet; UPPER glume is around 4.5–5.6 mm. Trace these to their actual base under 10–20×.

7. Distinguish the LOWER staminate/sterile floret and its conspicuously cross-veined membranous lemma from the UPPER fertile lemma, which ages hard, whitish and finely cross-ridged, without labeling these microscopic organs on unopened photos.
8. Compare 1-mm measured samples from U. fusca and U. reptans, NOT just whole-head photos: shorter spikelets and relatively smaller lower glumes, plus basal stem habit.
9. If species-specific lower glume, fertile lemma and true ligule are not resolved, report Urochloa sp. and retain provisional review.

10. Open USDA real PHOTO 6: TWO faces of the SAME U. texana spikelet. Left ventral lower glume/sterile lemma; right dorsal upper glume; actual original millimeter ticks visible. Remember these are alternate orientations, not two different grasses.
11. Open USDA real PHOTO 7: panels A/B are hard fertile FLORETS from dorsal/ventral side, C/D are actual removed GRAINS (caryopses). Scale is printed. None shows a true leaf ligule.

12. LIGULE source research-only: Clemson University U. texana page describes a genuine short membranous ciliate fringe, but its copyrighted image is NOT stored or reproduced. Collect a 1-mm lens photo from a Hays-vouchered plant before FINISHED.

13. WHOLE ROOT research-only: University of South Florida herbarium USF 192277 shows a real identified pressed flowering plant and fibrous roots; photo reproduction permission not verified, so only a link is provided. Need same-voucher local rooted plant.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Rank photos by what they truly show: flowering branch/shape first, followed by mature spikelet length and lower glume measured under 10–20×. Do not treat unmeasured photogenic heads as proof of native versus introduced species.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Source IDs and credited Commons photos do not establish county occurrence. Original gross arrows retained; glume/ligule microanatomy is NOT annotated in those images. Correction in detailed pass: Kew documents a 1–1.5mm ciliate membrane; UT Williamson plant description gives 1–1.8mm membranous BASE with fringe and white densely hairy COLLAR. Some broad keys summarize as 'ligule of hairs' but actual collar membrane must be photographed and labeled separately, not assumed identical to collar hairs. Lane 1 check: all four local source JPEGs verified; the two USDA plates are actual locally stored structures with source-marked mm scale. The remaining true ligule and connected Hays rooting-node view have no species-certified archived macro. All current look-alike panels now use independently licensed non-NC photographs. The public Learner still requires mobile/PAGES QA.

field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow a source-confirmed U. texana flowering stem to its rooted annual base; lower trailing nodes may root. At the INSIDE blade/sheath junction, distinguish the true truncate 1–1.8 mm ciliate membrane (UT; Kew 1–1.5 mm) from the adjacent white hairy collar (~1.5–2 mm); auricles absent in the UT description. NONE of the existing seven teaching panels actually photographs the opened TRUE inner ligule or a connected rooted flowering base. field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelet 4.5–5.9 mm; lower glume 2.4–3.2 mm, upper 4.5–5.6 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Use real USDA species panel 3 (index 2) for ventral/dorsal views with printed 1-mm ticks. UT reports lower glume (3)5–7-veined, reaching roughly the middle to two-thirds of the spikelet, and upper glume 5–7-veined and nearly full-length. The 322-pixel plate supports gross orientation/scale, not an invented fine vein-count arrow; take a sharper 10–20× dissection to confirm veins.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL ARCHIVED SCALED SPIKELET PLATE — HIGH-RES VEINS STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · TWO FLORETS; LEMMA, PALEA AND AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower staminate floret; upper fertile lemma ~3.5 mm, hardened, cross-ridged, without a long awn.
field_id_short_tiles.details: UT describes the lower floret's ~5-mm membranous five-veined lemma with conspicuous cross-veins and ~4-mm palea. Upper bisexual floret has a tough ~3.5 × 2.2-mm three-veined lemma and ~3.2-mm palea; Kew reports a rugose hardened fertile lemma with an apiculate tip, not a projecting long awn. USDA panel 4 (index 3) shows real fertile florets A/B and caryopses C/D; it does NOT show a leaf ligule or separately spread lower-floret lemma.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL USDA FERTILE FLORET PHOTO — LOWER-FLORET DISSECTION GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS SIGNALGRASS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Compare ripe spikelet LENGTH and lower-glume fraction, not just seedhead shape.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Texas U. texana: 4.5–5.9 mm, lower glume ~1/2–2/3; brownseed U. fusca: ~2.4–3.4 mm, lower glume ~1/4–1/3; creeping U. reptans: ~1.5–2.2 mm, lower glume ~1/8–1/4. Panels 5–7 (indices 4–6) are DIFFERENT-species photos; the previous panel 2 (index 1) was U. texana itself and belongs in the LOOK HERE FIRST lesson, not the look-alike-only photo selection. Southern crabgrass Digitaria ciliaris can have fingerlike racemes but a membranous rather than ciliate-membranous ligule; confirm under magnification. Unmeasured immature plants remain Urochloa sp.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL COMPARISON PHOTOS — MATCHED MILLIMETER SERIES MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE AND OWNER HANDOFF
